task: Phase 6 Step 8 -- Hirist JSON-LD normalization + job_url forensics, offline only, zero network requests

evidence_base.statement: The complete raw HTML and raw JSON-LD text from every live Hirist request (Steps 1, 4, and 7) was never persisted to any file in this project. Confirmed by grepping every data/reports/hirist_*.md and *.json file for JSON-LD markers before writing this report.
evidence_base.fragment_source: data/reports/hirist_phase6_inspection.md (Phase 6 Step 1), repeated verbatim in the Step 2 offline design doc
evidence_base.fragment_truncated_after: the word 'Senior' inside the name string value
evidence_base.step7_data_type: derived/aggregate parser output only (counts, final normalized company/title/job_url values) -- not raw captures

A_job_title.reliability_caveat: at least 1/26 normalized entries confirmed wrong (see delimiter_deep_dive)

B_company_name.confidence: FACT (Step 7: all 24 real jobs have a company)
B_company_name.reliability_caveat: shares the same wrong-split risk as title -- one bad split corrupts both fields together

C_job_url.explanation_status: NOT-DETERMINABLE which of two hypotheses is correct -- see job_url_deep_dive

D_location.code_reason: only set from nested item.jobLocation; flat path (the only path real data exercises) never sets it

E_experience.confidence: FACT -- never observed at all, and confirmed by new test C to never be assigned by any code path (nested or flat), including when experienceRequirements is present in a synthetic nested item

F_salary.confidence: FACT -- never observed, and confirmed by new test C to never be extracted by any code path

G_job_description.confidence: FACT (Step 7: all 24 real jobs took the flat path, which never sets jd_text)
G_job_description.code_support_exists_but_unexercised: nested_item.get('description') -- confirmed unexercised by real data

H_pagination.confidence: FACT (Step 7: rel=next correctly detected and followed across all 3 real pages)
H_pagination.status: the one field/capability with no open question

I_stable_job_identifier.confidence: FACT -- no url, @id, or any identifier populated for any of the 24 real jobs
I_stable_job_identifier.fallback_used_by_adapter: in-memory (company, title) tuple for cross-page dedup -- an approximation, not a true stable ID, and only as reliable as the confirmed-imperfect delimiter split

J_application_url.confidence: FACT -- confirmed by new test B: application_url is only ever set to '' in _empty_raw_job() and never assigned anywhere else in _parse_job_entry(), for either extraction path

delimiter_deep_dive.reproduction_confirmed_by: new test D -- feeding '"Senior DevOps Engineer - AWS & Kubernetes"' deterministically produces company='Senior DevOps Engineer', title='AWS & Kubernetes'

why_it_happens.hypothesis: the flat-name branch assumes every name follows 'Company - Title'; the bad entry is consistent with a different, equally plausible convention 'Title - Skills/Tags', but the actual raw name string for that entry was never captured, so this cannot be confirmed

alternatives_considered_and_rejected.alternative: use the nested item object instead of the flat name split
alternatives_considered_and_rejected.rejected_because: Step 7 confirms real data never populates the nested shape at all (0/24 jobs) -- not an alternative, a no-op

alternatives_considered_and_rejected.alternative: detect convention via keyword/position heuristics (e.g. 'if second segment looks like a skills list, swap it')
alternatives_considered_and_rejected.rejected_because: explicitly forbidden by task instructions as heuristic guessing to make output look better; no labeled examples of both conventions exist to validate against (only one bad example known)

alternatives_considered_and_rejected.alternative: reject entries where the split looks wrong
alternatives_considered_and_rejected.rejected_because: would require fabricating a rule to distinguish 'wrong split' from 'correct split with an unusual title' without further evidence

delimiter_deep_dive.conclusion: no deterministic, evidence-backed alternative exists with current evidence -- documented as an unresolved limitation, not fixed

scope_of_problem.reason: the 34 entries skipped for zero-or-multiple delimiter occurrences were never individually inspected or logged beyond the aggregate count

code_read_confirms.nested_branch_reads: nested_item.get('url') -- a url key INSIDE a nested 'item' sub-object (hirist_parser.py lines 262-297)
code_read_confirms.confirmed_by_test: new test A -- a synthetic flat-name ListItem with url, @id, and sameAs all set at the top level still produces job_url == ''

two_hypotheses.hypothesis: Hirist's real search-results JSON-LD genuinely does not include any per-item URL -- ListItem entries may only ever carry @type, position, and name; the actual job URL may only exist on a (never-fetched) detail page
two_hypotheses.plausibility: consistent with the one real fragment we have (shows exactly these three keys before truncation)
two_hypotheses.why_not_confirmable: the fragment is truncated -- cannot see whether more keys followed 'name' in the same object

two_hypotheses.hypothesis: a URL-shaped field exists in the real data but at a key/location the current code doesn't check -- e.g. a top-level 'url' or '@id' on the ListItem itself, sibling to 'name', rather than nested inside an 'item' object
two_hypotheses.plausibility: consistent with schema.org's own ItemList conventions, where ListItem.url (sibling to name) is a legitimate, commonly-used alternative to nesting a full item object
two_hypotheses.why_not_confirmable: raw JSON-LD was never persisted past what the parser extracted; the parser was never instrumented to log keys seen but not consumed during the Step 7 run

job_url_deep_dive.which_hypothesis_correct: NOT-DETERMINABLE from current evidence -- both remain live possibilities
what_would_be_needed_to_distinguish: a fresh, explicitly-authorized live capture with the RAW JSON-LD text persisted to a file (not just derived/normalized output)
OR instrumenting the parser to log all top-level keys seen on ListItem objects during a live run
job_url_deep_dive.reason_not_performed: explicit 'offline only, no further live query' instruction
job_url_deep_dive.fix_if_hypothesis_ii_correct: one-line addition to the flat-name branch: _sane_url_or_none(list_item.get('url') or list_item.get('@id')) before falling back to empty -- NOT implemented in this task, would be guessing at an unconfirmed hypothesis
job_url_deep_dive.fix_if_hypothesis_i_correct: no parser-level fix possible -- would require a new, separately-authorized per-job detail-page fetch (significant scope increase requiring its own inspection, robots.txt review, and rate-limit design)

ListItem_with_position.basis: FACT -- Step 1 fragment + Step 7 per-page counts

flat_name_string_on_ListItem.basis: FACT -- Step 1 fragment; Step 7 (100% of 24 parsed jobs used this path)

nested_item_object.basis: Step 7 positively suggests absence -- 0/24 real jobs took the nested path; report's own conclusion: 'Hirist's real search-results JSON-LD does not appear to use the nested-object shape at all'

top_level_url_at_id_sameAs_on_ListItem.basis: never checked for by the parser, never ruled out by any capture -- central open question of this report

JobPosting_fields_hiringOrganization_dat.basis: only ever read from the unconfirmed, apparently-unused nested-item path

assumption_discipline.instruction: Do not assume fields exist merely because Schema.org supports them
assumption_discipline.compliance: every 'not confirmed' row in schema_org_construct_review is treated as unconfirmed, not assumed present; no code change was made based on any unconfirmed field

new_characterization_tests.justification: evidence-justified per task instruction (not added merely for prettier output) -- each test pins a specific code-level gap identified in this forensic pass to a concrete, runnable, offline example

checks.proves: flat-name path ignores top-level url/@id/sameAs entirely -- confirms job_url_deep_dive hypothesis (ii)'s code-level mechanism
application_url is never populated by either extraction path -- confirms category J
baseSalary/experienceRequirements never read by any code path despite docstring listing baseSalary -- confirms categories E, F and the docstring/code mismatch
the ' - ' delimiter split reproduces Step 7's exact wrong-split result on a synthetic input -- confirms delimiter_deep_dive's reproducibility finding

new_characterization_tests.fix_deliberately_withheld_per_instructio: Do NOT fix the parser merely to make the test output prettier. If the evidence shows that company/title or job_url cannot currently be extracted reliably, document the limitation and stop.

summary: the flat 'Company - Title' delimiter split is not 100% reliable, reproduced deterministically in a new test; no deterministic evidence-backed alternative exists

job_url (and application_url, salary, experience) cannot currently be extracted reliably; two plausible, mutually exclusive explanations exist and cannot be distinguished without a new live capture that persists raw payload text
both limitations are documented, not fixed, per explicit instruction
